newsitem.title: USA: Ford denies report of executive changes.
newsitem.headline: Ford denies report of executive changes.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. Friday denied a report by Fortune magazine that Ford's board of directors has decided to bypass Edward Hagenlocker as the automaker's next chairman and chief executive officer.

David Scott, Ford's vice president of public affairs, also denied Fortune's report that the automaker has decided to replace Hagenlocker as president of Ford Automotive Operations with Jacques Nasser, the company's product development chief.

Fortune, in a press release Friday, said its October 14 issue also will report that the board has asked Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Alex Trotman to stay on past his 65th birthday in July 1998 and that 39-year-old William Clay Ford Jr. is a candidate to become the automaker's next chairman.
The press release did not identify Fortune's sources for the information.

"There are a lot of people who like the sport of speculating about management succession at Ford," Scott said in a statement responding to the press release. "In fact, we're getting quite used to it. However, we're not going to comment on speculation."
